gen.title: How increased distance from Earth center reduces weight
gen.orderNote: Steps follow the page order from surface distance to altitude weight result

steps.label: distance is about 4000 miles
steps.quote: On the surface of the earth the distance is about 4000 miles.
steps.orderHint: Track how growing distance lowers the weight value

steps.label: decrease with altitude
steps.quote: we would expect that the weight of an object would decrease with altitude.

steps.label: distance to the center of the earth is about 4007 miles
steps.quote: If an airplane is flying at 35000 feet (about 7 miles) the distance to the center of the earth is about 4007 miles.

steps.label: square of (4000/4007) which equals .9965
steps.quote: We can calculate the change in the gravitational constant as the square of (4000/4007) which equals .9965.

steps.label: weighs 9965 pounds at 35000 feet
steps.quote: If the airplane weighs 10000 pounds on the surface of the earth, it weighs 9965 pounds at 35000 feet; it has lost 35 pounds
